Investors must weigh these recent fundamental improvements against a multi-year track record of shrinking profits and sales [E17, E18, E55].

However, the market is currently undervaluing the company's assets, as evidenced by a P/B ratio of 1.53x, which is nearly half the sector benchmark of 3.03x [E7]. This valuation gap suggests that the market has not yet fully priced in the recent, robust recovery in sales and profit performance [E62, E64]. By fixating on historical stagnation, the bear overlooks the clear signal that the company is currently outperforming expectations [E52].

The bull’s reliance on a 105% profit growth figure [E19] ignores the broader context of a five-year compounded profit decline of -9% [E17] and a three-year decline of -4% [E18], suggesting that recent performance is a volatile recovery rather than a sustainable trend. While the bull points to a "fundamentals-led" environment [E52], this is directly contradicted by the scanX signal engine explicitly flagging that earnings growth is currently decelerating [E65]. The valuation argument based on a P/B ratio of 1.53x [E7] fails to justify the extreme P/E ratio of 64.3x [E1], which is nearly double the sector benchmark of 32.53x [E6]. However, these short-term metrics do not mitigate the long-term structural weakness of a -24.6% sales growth over the past five years [E55]. Furthermore, the lack of any dividend yield [E4] provides no income cushion for investors while they wait for this highly priced, historically stagnant business to prove its recent growth is not merely a temporary anomaly.
